title: HTML and CSS reference
summary: Tags and CSS you can click to insert, with what each one does.

items.label: <h1> heading
items.hint: The biggest heading. Use it once for the page title.

items.label: <h2> subheading
items.hint: A smaller heading for a section.
items.shows: A smaller heading under the title

items.label: paragraph
items.hint: A paragraph of text.
items.shows: Two paragraphs, with a gap between

items.label: <div> box
items.hint: A container that groups things together, so you can style them as one.

items.label: <ul> list
items.hint: A bulleted list. Each item is an <li>.

items.label: <ol> numbered list
items.hint: A numbered list.

items.label: comment
items.hint: A note that the browser ignores.
items.example: You can see this.

items.label: <a> link
items.hint: A link. The address goes in href; the words between the tags are what people click.
items.shows: The link text is blue and underlined

items.label: image
items.hint: A picture. src is the picture file; alt describes it for people who cannot see it. There is no closing tag.
items.example: Second place

items.label: <strong> bold
items.hint: Make text stand out as important (usually bold).
items.shows: Only the word inside is bold

items.label: <em> emphasis
items.hint: Emphasise text (usually italic).
items.shows: Only the word inside is italic

items.label: <button>
items.hint: A button.

items.label: line break
items.hint: Start a new line.
items.shows: A new line inside one paragraph

items.label: <hr> line
items.hint: Draw a line across the page.

items.label: <table>
items.hint: A table: <tr> is a row, <th> a heading cell, <td> a normal cell.
items.shows: Headings in bold, one row per <tr>

items.label: <header>
items.hint: The top part of a page: usually the title and the menu. Looks like a div; the name tells browsers and screen readers what it is.
items.shows: It looks like any block: the name is the difference

items.label: <nav>
items.hint: The main menu of links.

items.label: <main>
items.hint: The main content of the page. One per page.

items.label: <section>
items.hint: One part of the page, usually with its own heading.
items.shows: One part of a page with its heading

items.label: <footer>
items.hint: The bottom part of a page: contact details, small print.

items.label: <form>
items.hint: Holds the fields and the button that sends them. On its own, a form sends nowhere: code behind it does the work.

items.label: label and input
items.hint: An input is a box to type in. Its label says what to type; for and id must match, so clicking the label puts the cursor in the box.
items.shows: A labelled box for a number

items.label: <select> drop-down
items.hint: A drop-down list: one option to choose.
items.shows: A drop-down showing its first option

items.label: <style> block
items.hint: Where CSS lives. Each rule is: selector { property: value; }

items.label: rule
items.hint: Style every element matching the selector.

items.label: class selector
items.hint: Style only the elements you mark with class="note" in the HTML. The dot is only in the CSS.
items.example:
A normal paragraph.

A paragraph with class="tip".
items.shows: Only the paragraph with the class changes

items.label: several selectors
items.hint: One rule for several kinds of element: list the selectors with commas.
items.example:
Title

  • An item

A paragraph
items.shows: The heading and the list item change; the paragraph does not

items.label: color
items.hint: The text colour.

items.label: background-color
items.hint: The background colour.

items.label: font-size
items.hint: How big the text is.

items.label: font-family
items.hint: Which font to use.

items.label: text-align
items.hint: Align text: left, center or right.
items.shows: The heading moves to the middle

items.label: display: flex
items.hint: Put it on the box that holds the items (the parent): its children line up in a row.
items.shows: The three paragraphs sit side by side

items.label: gap
items.hint: Space between the items in a flex row (on the parent, with display: flex).

items.label: flex-wrap
items.hint: Let items move to the next line when the row is full.
items.shows: The fourth star wraps to the next line

items.label: justify-content
items.hint: Where the items sit along the row: flex-start, center, flex-end or space-between.
items.example:
Left

Right
items.shows: space-between pushes the items to the ends

items.label: list-style
items.hint: Remove the bullets or numbers from a list: menus are lists without bullets.

items.label: display: grid
items.hint: Put it on the box that holds the items: its children are placed in rows and columns (with grid-template-columns).
items.example:
A

B

C

D

items.label: grid-template-columns
items.hint: The width of each column, in order. 1fr means one share of the space left; repeat(3, 1fr) makes three equal columns.
items.example:
80px
The rest
items.shows: A fixed column, then one that takes the rest

items.label: width
items.hint: How wide the content is. Padding and border are added on top of it.
items.example: A box 120 pixels wide

items.label: padding
items.hint: Space inside an element, between its edge and its content.
items.shows: Space between the edge and the text

items.label: margin
items.hint: Space outside an element, between it and its neighbours.

items.label: border
items.hint: A line around an element: thickness, style, colour.

items.label: on click
items.hint: When the element with id="go" is clicked, run the lines inside. # means id, as . means class.

items.label: change the text
items.hint: Replace the words inside the element with id="message".

items.label: read a box
items.hint: Read what someone typed into the box with id="name".
